verdict.line: You lose if you let him stack Siphoning Strike uncontested and melee him after his ult; you win if you poke him down with Parrrley before level 6 and keep him off his stacks.

brief.thesis: Parrrley has 625 range and Siphoning Strike only reaches 255, so Nasus physically cannot answer your poke until he either flashes in or lands enough Q stacks to force a trade. The entire lane is about denying him free Siphoning Strike casts on minions while chipping him down at a range he can't match.

theirWindow.when: Level 6+, he presses Fury of the Sands
theirWindow.what: His health, range, and damage spike while the ult is active (120s cooldown). Do not extend a melee trade into it — disengage and let it run out before reapproaching.

yourWindow.when: He commits Siphoning Strike at a minion
yourWindow.what: The cast locks him in place at 255 range. Walk up and land a free Parrrley or auto for passive poison stacks while he's recovering.

start.why: The lifesteal and HP sustain let you win extended poke exchanges where Nasus is forced to eat Parrrley hits without being able to Q back.

boots.why: Nasus's threat comes from auto attacks and Siphoning Strike procs; the flat auto-damage reduction blunts both his CS'd Q and any all-in he lands after a Wither.

core.why: Mana sustain to spam Parrrley all lane without running dry, which is how you keep outranging him
Lowers the execute threshold — Parrrley killing blows already grant bonus gold and a mana refund, and Collector stacks that reward on top
Cuts through the armor Nasus naturally stacks as he tanks up, keeping your poke relevant into the late game

situational.when: he builds lifesteal or healing to lean harder on Soul Eater
he is threatening to kill you outright in a single all-in after Fury of the Sands
the game runs long and he isn't stacking armor, so raw crit outvalues armor pen

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacks a second damage-over-time on top of your Grog-Soaked Blade poison, which matters because Nasus can't rush you down fast enough at 255 range to punish a DOT-heavy poke trade.

summoners.why: Ignite converts your Parrrley poke into kill pressure and cuts into the lifesteal he gets from Soul Eater during any extended trade.

playing.title: Poke at max range
playing.detail: Use Parrrley at 625 range to harass; Siphoning Strike only reaches 255, so he cannot answer without walking into your attack range first.

playing.title: Cleanse Wither on sight
playing.detail: The moment he lands Wither, use Remove Scurvy to clear the slow and heal, restoring the kiting distance his whole kit depends on removing.

playing.title: Punish his CS windups
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike's cooldown drops from 8s to 4s as he ranks it, but every cast still locks him in place on a minion — that's a free Parrrley or auto window.

playing.title: Respect level 6 Fury of the Sands
playing.detail: Once his ult (120s cooldown) is up, don't extend melee trades into it. Back off and let the duration expire before re-engaging.

playing.title: Never stand in Spirit Fire
playing.detail: His 650 range, 12s cooldown zone shreds armor on anyone standing in it. Don't contest CS or trade inside it, even for a last hit.

playing.title: Use Raise Morale to extend or escape
playing.detail: The 1200 range, 20s cooldown AD and movement speed buff lets you either commit harder to a trade or physically outrun his melee kit on disengage.

playing.title: Save Parrrley to execute
playing.detail: A killing blow with Parrrley grants bonus gold and refunds half its mana cost, so hold it to finish low-health trades rather than opening with it.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win rates are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade timing are my own read of the matchup.

stats.opponentTip: Focus on getting control over lane during early game. Be careful when he uses Unbound Spellbook - (R) to get a kill. Always use [W] to his (W) to manage your distance well.
